summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas Search Architecture. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Atlas Search uses a Lucene-based mongot process for search indexing and execution. Its term-based index is inverted: a term identifies documents containing it. (high confidence)

For sharded collections, mongos distributes search queries across shards and gathers results. The documented routing scopes queries to shards containing the collection when zone placement confines that collection to a subset. (low confidence)

For sharded collections, search is distributed across shards containing the collection; mongos gathers results rather than allowing a search query to target an arbitrary single shard. Dedicated Search Nodes are provisioned per shard. (high confidence)

The AWS and MongoDB engineering account describes accelerating search-node rebuilding by downloading a recent Lucene file snapshot from S3 instead of always rescanning the complete source collection. Current Atlas documentation scopes snapshot reuse to eligible dedicated Search Nodes without customer key management. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
Atlas Search separates Lucene-backed search indexing and matching in mongot from MongoDB document storage and ordinary database processing in mongod. (high confidence)
In the normal query path, mongot searches and scores matches, then returns document IDs and metadata to mongod; mongod retrieves the matching collection documents for the response. (high confidence)

Search indexing consumes MongoDB change streams asynchronously and provides eventual consistency; an acknowledged collection write does not guarantee immediate visibility to a search query. (high confidence)

Atlas supports colocating mongot and mongod on the same nodes or running mongot on dedicated Search Nodes. Dedicated nodes separate their compute resources and allow search capacity to scale independently of database capacity. (high confidence)

An index’s storedSource setting can retain selected fields in mongot. A query using returnStoredSource can retrieve those fields directly and avoid the usual full-document lookup in mongod. (high confidence)
For dedicated Search Nodes, mongod normally sends search queries through a local load balancer that distributes requests across mongot processes. (low confidence)

An ADEO engineering article demonstrates an indexing race in local integration tests: inserting documents and immediately issuing a search can run before asynchronous search indexing finishes. (medium confidence)

A Kuali reproduction repository reports that persisting mongodb-atlas-local search state across container restarts requires considering /data/mongot alongside /data/db and /data/configdb; its mounted-volume failures concern local deployment behavior. (low confidence)
In the colocated deployment model, mongot runs alongside mongod on each database node and shares that node’s resources. (high confidence)
Dedicated Search Nodes run mongot separately from database nodes. This isolates search resources and lets search capacity scale independently of the database. (high confidence)
